mechanism: Larry Williams nested swings: short-term low = bar low flanked by higher lows; short-term high = bar high flanked by lower highs. Intermediate low = short-term low lower than flanking short-term lows; intermediate high = short-term high higher than flanking short-term highs. EA reads four indicator buffers (shortTermLows/Highs, intermediateTermLows/Highs) via CopyBuffer and treats nested structure as the objective market-structure regime.
data_needed: larryWilliamsMarketStructureIndicator buffers 0–3; ArraySetAsSeries; refresh on new bar via IsNewBar(iTime)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: chart _Symbol; input ENUM_TIMEFRAMES timeframe=PERIOD_CURRENT; backtest Gold H1 2025-01-01 to 2025-11-30
why_new_for_mis: Mechanical nested short→intermediate swing stack is a reusable multi-scale structure-regime sensor without discretionary ringed highs/lows.
quote: An intermediate-term low is a short-term low that is lower than the short-term lows on both sides. An intermediate-term high is a short-term high that is higher than the short-term highs on both sides.

mechanism: Buy only when shortTermLows[2] is non-EMPTY and the next prior short-term low index also has intermediateTermLows[commonIndex] non-EMPTY (short-term low confirming an intermediate low). Sell mirrors with shortTermHighs and intermediateTermHighs. Evaluated once per new bar after RefreshMarketStructureBuffers—emits a discrete structure-confirmation event for corrective-phase end / new leg start.
data_needed: short/intermediate swing buffers; index scan from bar 3; new-bar gate
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol on selected timeframe; Gold H1 backtest cited
why_new_for_mis: Confirmation-of-higher-swing-by-lower-swing is an explicit nested-structure change event MIS can stream alongside other regime flips.
quote: A long position is opened when a short-term swing low confirms an intermediate-term swing low. This suggests that price has likely completed a corrective phase and may be entering a new upward leg.

mechanism: Stop placed at user-chosen short-term or intermediate swing extreme. stopDistance = |entry − stopLevel|; reject trade if stopDistance outside [minimumStopDistancePoints, maximumStopDistancePoints] × SYMBOL_POINT. Filters structure setups that are too tight (noise) or too wide (poor risk) as a structure-implied volatility/range gate.
data_needed: shortTermLows/Highs[2] or nearest intermediate swing; SYMBOL_POINT; min/max points inputs (defaults 100/600)

quote: To control this, the user defines a minimum and maximum allowed stop distance in points. Any trade that falls outside this range is ignored. This protects the EA from entering trades with poor risk characteristics.

mechanism: Article encodes Williams’ claim that swing points are actionable support/resistance: when they hold they confirm trend continuation; when they break they warn of trend change. EA operationalizes the hold/confirm path via nested confirmation entries and structure-based stops at those swings.
data_needed: confirmed short/intermediate swing levels; price relative to swing extreme

why_new_for_mis: Frames swing extremes as binary hold/break regime-change sensors tied to nested structure, not generic S/R.
quote: When they hold, they confirm trend continuation. When they break, they warn of a trend change.

mechanism: On new bar, inspect bars 1–3: swing low if low2<low1 and low2<low3; swing high if high2>high1 and high2>high3. Store lwShortTermSwingLevel = low2/high2. Self-contained EA (no external indicator) detects micro-structure rhythm of short-term extremes as the smallest reactive market-structure layer.
data_needed: iHigh/iLow for indices 1,2,3; IsNewBar; global lwShortTermSwingLevel
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: input timeframe PERIOD_CURRENT; daily backtests Gold, S&P500, Bitcoin, GBPUSD 2024-01-01 to 2025-11-30
why_new_for_mis: Compact three-bar pivot sensor with stored structural extreme gives MIS a portable short-horizon structure regime flag across asset classes.
quote: These short-term highs and lows form the smallest, most reactive layer of market structure, acting as the building blocks from which intermediate and long-term trends emerge.

mechanism: After candidate swing at bar 2, reject if bar 2 is an outside bar vs bar 3: (high2>high3)&&(low2<low3). Outside bars engulf neighbors and are treated as excessive volatility/instability that distorts natural swing rhythm—not controlled exhaustion.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: same multi-asset daily tests; any TF via EA input
why_new_for_mis: Explicit outside-bar volatility veto on swing candidates is a structure-quality filter MIS can reuse whenever pivots are mined.
quote: Outside bars, by definition, encompass the surrounding bars and introduce excessive volatility. Rather than signaling controlled exhaustion, they reflect instability and imbalance.

mechanism: Reject swing if bar 1 is an inside bar relative to bar 2: (high1<high2)&&(low1>low2). Inside bars mark contraction/indecision lacking participant commitment; Williams filters them so only explicit short-term intent remains.
why_new_for_mis: Inside-bar adjacency as a contraction/indecision veto pairs with outside-bar volatility veto for a two-sided bar-range regime filter on pivots.
quote: An inside bar represents contraction and indecision, not resolution. When a swing candidate forms on or adjacent to an inside bar, the structure lacks market participants' commitment.
